---
title: "Getting started with Open Data Standards"
---

Use this guide to prepare data and metadata for Explore Education Statistics
(EES). It follows a straightforward dataset with time, geography, filters and
indicators. You can work in a spreadsheet, R, Python or another tool.

The [Open Data Standards](ud.qmd) are the full reference, including exceptions
and accepted values. Requirements for the
[EES API](api-data-standards.qmd) apply in addition to those standards.

## 1. Know what you need to produce

Prepare these together:

::: {.table-responsive tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Required outputs"}

| Output | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Data CSV, for example `pupil-enrolments.csv` | Contains publishable observations. EES uses it for tables and charts, and users can download it. |
| EES metadata CSV, `pupil-enrolments.meta.csv` | Describes the filters and indicators, including the labels, units and precision shown to users. The filename matches the data file with `.meta` added. |
| Public data guidance and methodology | Explain coverage, definitions, denominators, limitations and methods. These are separate from the metadata CSV. Follow the [public data guidance instructions](ees.qmd#public-data-guidance). |

:::

Everything in the downloadable data must be suitable for publication. Apply
your disclosure control policy to the data itself; changing display precision
in metadata does not hide the underlying values.

If you intend to publish through the API, start the
[API publishing checklist](api-data-standards.qmd#api-publishing-checklist)
early. Passing automated checks alone does not grant API approval.

## 2. Identify what one row represents {#worked-example}

Before changing the data, describe one row: **[measures] for [group] in [place]
during [period].**

In this example, each row gives a pupil count and percentage for one education
phase, sex, location and academic year.

The figures are **synthetic**, not official statistics. They cover primary and
secondary pupils, classified as male or female, in all nine English regions.
Each pupil belongs to one region and one phase. Real data may have other
categories, different coverage or suppressed values. Keep those differences
when adapting the example.

Download the [wide source CSV](../resources/open-data-standards/pupil-source.csv).
It has 18 rows: two years and nine regions. Four columns hold counts for male
primary, male secondary, female primary and female secondary pupils. The source
has region names but no region codes. Here is an extract:

::: {.table-responsive tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Source data extract"}

```{r echo=FALSE}
#| output: asis
source_data <- read.csv("../resources/open-data-standards/pupil-source.csv",
                        colClasses = "character", check.names = FALSE)
example_data <- read.csv("../resources/open-data-standards/pupil-enrolments.csv",
                         colClasses = "character", check.names = FALSE)
example_meta <- read.csv("../resources/open-data-standards/pupil-enrolments.meta.csv",
                         colClasses = "character", check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(head(source_data, 2), row.names = FALSE, caption = "Source extract: North East, 2022/23.")
```

:::

Identify the role of each column before transforming it:

::: {.table-responsive tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Column roles"}

| Role | Example | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| Time | Academic year 2022/23 | Use `time_period` of `202223` and `time_identifier` of `Academic year`. |
| Geography | North East | Match the name to a standard region code, then add `geographic_level`, country code and country name. |
| Filters | Primary/secondary; male/female | Take education phase and sex from the four source column names and give each its own column. |
| Indicators | Pupil count; pupil percentage | Put the four source counts into one `pupil_count` column. Calculate `pupil_percent` after adding totals. |

:::

## 3. Choose a structure that supports your users

Move the four count columns into one `pupil_count` column. Add separate `sex`
and `education_phase` filters so users can select, for example, female primary
pupils. A combined “Female primary” category would prevent users from selecting
sex and phase independently.

Keep counts and percentages in the same file because they describe the same
groups and users may want them in one table. EES tables draw from one data
file. For incompatible measures or filters, use the
[dataset design decisions](ud.qmd#dataset-design-decisions).

Calculate totals from groups that do not overlap. In this example:

- Add male and female counts to obtain `sex = Total` for each phase.
- Add primary and secondary counts to obtain `education_phase = All education phases`.
- Add the nine equivalent regional counts to obtain national counts.

Do not add a total to the rows that make it up, or add national rows to regional
rows. Overlapping categories, rates and averages may need other methods. Do not
add percentages to produce totals.

Here `pupil_percent` means the percentage of pupils of the selected sex
**within the same year, geography and education phase**. Divide that row's
count by the corresponding `sex = Total` count and multiply by 100. For
North East primary pupils in 2022/23, this is 13,100 / 25,000 × 100 = 52.4
for males. Explain the denominator in public data guidance.

## 4. Prepare the data CSV

Use the exact [mandatory time and geography columns](ud.qmd#time-and-geography):
`time_period`, `time_identifier`, `geographic_level`, `country_code` and
`country_name`. Add the [columns needed for your geography levels](ud.qmd#allowable-geographic-levels).
This example also needs `region_code` and `region_name`; those cells are
empty on national rows because a region is not applicable to them. The R script
matches each source region name to a code using
[dfeR's `fetch_regions()` lookup](https://dfe-analytical-services.github.io/dfeR/reference/fetch_regions.html).
Check every name matched before producing the file. The Python script uses a
[CSV copy of those nine lookup entries](../resources/open-data-standards/pupil-region-lookup.csv)
exported from dfeR.

Use [harmonised names and categories](ud.qmd#common-harmonised-variables),
including `sex` and `education_phase`. The harmonised phase total is
`All education phases`. Follow [variable naming](ud.qmd#variable-names)
and [indicator naming](ud.qmd#indicator-names) guidance for other columns.

The [finished data CSV](../resources/open-data-standards/pupil-enrolments.csv)
has 180 rows: two years × ten locations (nine regions and England) × three
phase categories × three sex categories. This extract omits the time and
geography columns to show the reshaping:

::: {.table-responsive tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Finished data extract"}

```{r echo=FALSE}
#| output: asis
extract <- example_data[example_data$time_period == "202223" &
                        example_data$region_code == "E12000001", ]
knitr::kable(extract[, c("education_phase", "sex", "pupil_count", "pupil_percent")],
             row.names = FALSE, caption = "Finished data extract: North East, 2022/23.")
```

:::

Save as [UTF-8 CSV](ud.qmd#how-to-export-data-with-utf-8-encoding) with one
header row, no title rows and no row-number column. Preserve geography codes
as text. Reopen the exported CSV to check its contents, including leading
zeros where relevant. Store a percentage such as 52.4% as `52.4`, with `%`
in metadata, not `0.524` or the text `52.4%`.

This example has no missing or suppressed observations. In real data use the
[specified symbols](ud.qmd#data-symbols): for example, `c` for a confidential
count, `x` for an unavailable observation and `z` for a measure that does not
apply. Do not substitute zero for these. If a suppressed count can be
recovered from a percentage or total, apply your publication's disclosure
control policy to those values too. The example's calculation code assumes
complete numeric counts and is not a disclosure control routine.

## 5. Create the metadata {#create-the-metadata}

Download the [matching metadata CSV](../resources/open-data-standards/pupil-enrolments.meta.csv).
It contains one row for each of the two filters and two indicators. These are
the settings which affect this example's display:

::: {.table-responsive tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Metadata settings"}

```{r echo=FALSE}
#| output: asis
knitr::kable(example_meta[, c("col_name", "col_type", "label", "indicator_unit",
                              "indicator_dp", "filter_default")],
             row.names = FALSE, caption = "Selected metadata columns; the download contains every required header.")
```

:::

Include **all eight [mandatory metadata headers](ud.qmd#mandatory-ees-metadata-columns)**,
even when cells are empty. Copy each `col_name` exactly from the data header.
Set `col_type` to `Filter` or `Indicator` and give every row a readable `label`.

For this example:

- Counts leave `indicator_unit` empty and set `indicator_dp = 0`. Percentages
  use `%` and `indicator_dp = 1`. The downloaded values are rounded to at most
  three decimal places; EES displays one.
- The filter rows leave indicator settings empty. The indicator rows leave
  filter settings empty. `indicator_grouping` and `filter_grouping_column`
  are empty because this example does not use grouping.
- The optional `filter_default` column selects `All education phases` for the
  phase filter and `Total` for sex. See [defaults and their hierarchy restriction](ud.qmd#aggregates-and-default-filters).
- Standard time and geography columns have no metadata rows. A filter with
  only one value also has no metadata row. A column used only to group another
  filter is referenced in `filter_grouping_column`, not given a separate row.

### Reproduce the example in R or Python

Put the source CSV and either the [R script](../resources/open-data-standards/prepare-pupil-example.R)
or [Python script](../resources/open-data-standards/prepare-pupil-example.py)
in one folder. The R script needs `dfeR`, `dplyr` and `tidyr` installed. For
Python, also download the [region lookup CSV](../resources/open-data-standards/pupil-region-lookup.csv);
the script uses only Python's standard library. Run your chosen script from
that folder. It writes `pupil-enrolments.csv` and `pupil-enrolments.meta.csv`,
replacing files with those names.

```bash
Rscript --vanilla prepare-pupil-example.R
```

Or:

```bash
python prepare-pupil-example.py
```

Read the comments before adapting the scripts. They assume the source's
coverage and categories, and do not handle missing or suppressed values.

## 6. Validate the pair and resolve problems

Run **both files** through the [EES screening app](https://rsconnect/rsc/dfe-published-data-qa/)
before upload. This requires access from DfE kit. Keep the results with your
publication's quality assurance record. Fix reported problems in the source
or preparation code, regenerate both files as needed, and screen again.

Use the [validation and troubleshooting guide](ud.qmd#validation-and-troubleshooting)
to distinguish formatting errors from structural and statistical problems.
Investigate warnings as well as failures. A successful screen does not prove
that the figures, disclosure control or user experience are correct.

Reconcile counts with the source, check that totals use the right populations,
and recalculate a sample of percentages. The existing
[publication-specific automated sense checks](../RAP/common-rap-principles/publication-project-specific-automated-sense-checks.qmd)
guidance explains how to build these into your production process.

## 7. Check the experience in EES

After [uploading the screened files](ees.qmd#uploading-files), preview the
release and try the questions your users will ask. For this example:

- Make a table comparing male and female primary pupils across regions.
- Show a national time series without adding national and regional totals.
- Make a chart of percentages and check its labels, units and precision.
- Check the default selections and explain what each percentage measures.
- Download the data and check that the guidance explains how to avoid double counting.

For an existing publication, also check [replacing data](ees.qmd#replacing-data)
before changing column names or structures used by existing data blocks.

For API publication, complete the [additional checks and manual approval](api-data-standards.qmd#api-publishing-checklist).
Keep filter and indicator labels within **80 characters**, even if a tool
accepts longer labels. Check harmonised dictionary entries and tell affected
users about changes to existing API datasets.

## First-publication checklist {#first-publication-checklist}

Use this checklist with your publication files. “Required” marks a standard or
publishing step; “Recommended” marks a useful check. Record what you checked in
your quality assurance record, including checks the screener cannot do.

::: {.table-responsive tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="First-publication checklist"}

| Done | Check and reference | Status | How to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| ☐ | All downloadable values meet disclosure control policy; [symbols](ud.qmd#data-symbols) distinguish missing, suppressed and zero values. | Required | Analyst judgement; screening can check recognised formats. |
| ☐ | Data and matching `.meta.csv` use [UTF-8 CSV and suitable filenames](ud.qmd#data-format). | Required | Inspect exports and screen the pair. |
| ☐ | Exact [mandatory fields and geography-specific columns](ud.qmd#time-and-geography) are present with appropriate values. | Required | Screening and a check of geographic coverage. |
| ☐ | Each row has a clear meaning; filters and indicators follow [tidy data principles](ud.qmd#tidy-data-structure). | Required | Analyst judgement; screening alone cannot decide the design. |
| ☐ | Names and categories follow [naming](ud.qmd#variable-names) and applicable [harmonisation](ud.qmd#common-harmonised-variables) guidance. | Required where specified | Screening and reference review. |
| ☐ | Metadata has [all required headers](ud.qmd#mandatory-ees-metadata-columns), exact matching names and appropriate rows. | Required | Screening and inspection. |
| ☐ | Counts reconcile; denominators, totals and [display precision](ud.qmd#indicators) are correct. | Recommended QA checks | Recalculate from source; inspect tables and downloads. |
| ☐ | The final pair has been [screened](ud.qmd#how-to-check-against-these-standards) and reported problems addressed. | Required | Run the app again after corrections; retain results. |
| ☐ | Intended tables, charts, defaults and downloads are understandable. | Recommended | Try representative user questions in EES. |
| ☐ | [Public data guidance](ees.qmd#public-data-guidance), methodology and normal sign-off are complete. | Required publishing steps | Analyst and approver review. |
| ☐ | [API limits](api-data-standards.qmd#character-limits-for-col_names-and-filter-items), dictionary entries, warnings, upload checks and manual activation have been addressed. | Required for API only | Automated checks plus platform team approval. |

:::
